alex: Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC: proposing a lightweight startup probe that sets SM-capability flags for A100 / H100 / L4 and picks optimized kernel paths. Goal is: deterministic, fast (<200ms), and safe (no crashes).

rina: Curious about the probe surface — what exact features do we detect? wmma/fp8/ptx/warp size/L2 size? Also worried about probes running on every container start (cost + noise). :eyes:

alex: Good q. Minimum set: sm_major/minor, ptx_version, support_wmma, support_tf32_accel, max_warp_size, L2_cache_kb. Optional: fp8_hw_support. We'll cache per-node and attach to node metadata so each host probes once.

jon: +1 for node-level cache. Also add driver version and cuda-runtime check — we've seen old drivers lie about wmma. If driver < N.N.N, force generic path.

sam: For L4 special-case: it often prefers smaller kernels with fewer registers. We should also detect compute capability that implies lower shared mem per SM and pick low-occupancy kernels. Also add a cheap microkernel that runs a tiny matmul to validate correctness of the optimized path.

alex: Agreed. Probe should have two phases: capability query via CUDA API, then optional microbench verification with a tiny matmul / attention-smoke that validates outputs within tolerance. Fail -> mark as incompatible.

morgan: Implementation nit: make the probe opt-out via env var (REDWOOD_SKIP_HW_PROBE=1) for debug/on-prem installs. Also emit telemetry: kernel_variant, probe_result, probe_version.

deploy-bot: [automated] canary rollout for runtime v2.8 scheduled at 2026-04-02T10:00Z (1% traffic)

rina: How does runtime decide at request time? policy should be: prefer most-optimized variant that is compatible and passes safety checks, otherwise fallback to generic path. We must avoid on-request blocking probes.

alex: Exactly. Selection algorithm (pseudocode):

```
if (node_probe.ok) {
  if (has_wmma && sm_major>=8 && driver_ok) use_h100_wmma_kern();
  elif (is_l4 && low_shared_mem) use_l4_lowreg_kern();
  elif (has_tf32_accel) use_typed_gemm_kern();
  else use_generic_kern();
} else {
  use_generic_kern();
}
```

jon: That pseudocode is fine but we should also track runtime metrics: fallback_count (per-hour), correctness_mismatch_rate, latency_p99_by_variant. If mismatch rate climbs, auto-disable variant via rollout policy.

sam: One more concern: kv-cache serialization/ABI. Some optimized kernels rely on specific layout (e.g., packed QKV with 128B alignment). If we switch kernels mid-rollout, ensure stash compatibility or provide upgrade path that invalidates old KV entries gracefully.

alex: Good catch. Plan: kernel-variant tag is part of session metadata; KV entries include variant_version. If variant changes incompatibly, we either migrate on read (cheap path) or fall back. Need a small migration utility in runtime.

morgan: Testing plan: microbench harness for each variant, nightly full-model regression on a couple representative models (2B, 70B), and a canary rollout with synthetic traffic that exercises long-sequence attention to catch KV/latency issues.

rina: Probe corner cases: VMs reboot with different GPU firmware or driver updates. TTL for cached node metadata should be short (24h) or invalidated on driver update event from infra. Also add a forced re-probe endpoint in the node agent.

alex: Agreed on TTL=24h default, force-reprobe API, and event hook from infra that clears cache on driver/gpu-firmware change.

jon: For safety, add a runtime flag to force-generic for a route: route_config.kernel_preference = "generic" for customers with strict determinism needs.

sam: Ops: add alert if fallback_count > 0.5% for more than 15m during canary. Also add regression guard: if p99 latency increases >15% on canary, auto-roll back.

morgan: I'll own the telemetry dashboard and alerts. alex and jon, can you split the work?

alex: I'll own probe implementation + node cache + env opt-out.

jon: I'll take selection policy + metrics + rollback hooks.

alex: Action items summarized: 1) probe binary + microbench (alex) 2) node metadata caching + TTL + reprobe API (alex) 3) selection policy impl + telemetry and rollback (jon) 4) KV variant tagging + migration plan (sam) 5) canary plan + dashboards (morgan).

rina: Also add docs in eng-runtime/README about safe defaults and how to opt out.

alex: I'll open RFC follow-up PR with code pointers and test checklist. Target: land core probe + telemetry in runtime v2.8 canary. :shipit: 

morgan: I'll schedule the canary smoke tests and create the dashboard widgets.

sam: One-liner: keep microbench deterministic and bounded (<200ms) or skip it. :shrug:

alex: Agreed — microbench should run with a strict timeout and be optional. If it times out, default to conservative flag (generic path).

morgan: I'll mark owners in the follow-up PR and add the alert rules.

alex: Thanks all — will post the PR link shortly and add the rollout timeline.

rina: Great. We'll iterate after canary metrics come in.
